1180 — Abū Namlah al-Anṣārī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
While he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and a Jewish man was also present, a funeral procession passed by.
The Jewish man asked:
“O Muḥammad, does this deceased person speak?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Allah knows best.”
The Jewish man said:
“It does speak.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said:
“Whatever the People of the Book relate to you, neither affirm it nor deny it. Say: ‘We believe in Allah and His Messengers.’ If what they say is false, you will not have affirmed it; and if it is true, you will not have denied it.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3644), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6257).

«بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً، وَحَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ، وَمَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٦١).

١١٨٥ — عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«حَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ؛ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَتْ فِيهِمُ الْأَعَاجِيبُ».
ثم أنشأ يحدث، قال:
خرجت طائفة من بني إسرائيل حتى أتوا مقبرة لهم من مقابرهم، فقالوا: لو صلينا ركعتين، ودعونا الله عز وجل أن يخرج لنا رجلًا ممن قد مات، نسأله عن الموت.
قال: ففعلوا.
فبينما هم كذلك إذ اطلع رجل رأسه من قبر من تلك المقابر، خُلاسيٌّ، بين عينيه أثر السجود، فقال:
يا هؤلاء، ما أردتم إليَّ؟ فقد مت منذ مائة سنة، فما سكنت عني حرارة الموت حتى كان الآن، فادعوا الله عز وجل لي أن يعيدني كما كنت.
حسن: رواه أحمد في الزهد (ص ٢٣)، وابن أبي شيبة في مسنده، كما في المطالب العالية (٧٧٤).
وقوله: «خرجت طائفة من بني إسرائيل» إلى آخره، ليس من قول النبي ﷺ، بل هو من قول جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما، كما جاء مصرحًا عند أحمد بن منيع في المطالب العالية (٣/٧٧٤). وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أنه من قول عبد الرحمن بن سابط.
وقوله: «خُلاسيٌّ»؛ الخُلْس: السمرة، ومنه صبي خُلاسي إذا كان بين أبيض وأسود.

1185 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm in doing so, for indeed there were wondrous events among them.”
Then he began narrating and said:
A group from the Children of Israel went out until they came to one of their graveyards. They said:
“If only we were to pray two rakʿahs and supplicate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to bring forth for us a man from among those who have died, so that we may ask him about death.”
So they did.
While they were in that state, a man raised his head from one of those graves. He was of a brownish complexion, and between his eyes was the mark of prostration.
He said:
“O people, what do you want from me? I died one hundred years ago, yet the heat of death did not cease from me until just now. So supplicate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to return me to the state in which I was.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad in al-Zuhd (p. 23) and Ibn Abī Shaybah in his Musnad, as cited in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (774).
The statement beginning, “A group from the Children of Israel went out…” through the end is not from the words of the Prophet ﷺ. Rather, it is from the words of Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh may Allah be pleased with them, as explicitly stated in the narration of Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (3/774). Some scholars held that it is instead from the words of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ.
The word khulāsī refers to a brownish complexion. A boy may be described as khulāsī when his complexion is between white and black.

١١٨٥ — عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«حَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ؛ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَتْ فِيهِمُ الْأَعَاجِيبُ».
ثم أنشأ يحدث، قال:
خرجت طائفة من بني إسرائيل حتى أتوا مقبرة لهم من مقابرهم، فقالوا: لو صلينا ركعتين، ودعونا الله عز وجل أن يخرج لنا رجلًا ممن قد مات، نسأله عن الموت.
قال: ففعلوا.
فبينما هم كذلك إذ اطلع رجل رأسه من قبر من تلك المقابر، خُلاسيٌّ، بين عينيه أثر السجود، فقال:
يا هؤلاء، ما أردتم إليَّ؟ فقد مت منذ مائة سنة، فما سكنت عني حرارة الموت حتى كان الآن، فادعوا الله عز وجل لي أن يعيدني كما كنت.
حسن: رواه أحمد في الزهد (ص ٢٣)، وابن أبي شيبة في مسنده، كما في المطالب العالية (٧٧٤).
وقوله: «خرجت طائفة من بني إسرائيل» إلى آخره، ليس من قول النبي ﷺ، بل هو من قول جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما، كما جاء مصرحًا عند أحمد بن منيع في المطالب العالية (٣/٧٧٤). وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أنه من قول عبد الرحمن بن سابط.
وقوله: «خُلاسيٌّ»؛ الخُلْس: السمرة، ومنه صبي خُلاسي إذا كان بين أبيض وأسود.
1185 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm in doing so, for indeed there were wondrous events among them.”
Then he began narrating and said:
A group from the Children of Israel went out until they came to one of their graveyards. They said:
“If only we were to pray two rakʿahs and supplicate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to bring forth for us a man from among those who have died, so that we may ask him about death.”
So they did.
While they were in that state, a man raised his head from one of those graves. He was of a brownish complexion, and between his eyes was the mark of prostration.
He said:
“O people, what do you want from me? I died one hundred years ago, yet the heat of death did not cease from me until just now. So supplicate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to return me to the state in which I was.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad in al-Zuhd (p. 23) and Ibn Abī Shaybah in his Musnad, as cited in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (774).
The statement beginning, “A group from the Children of Israel went out…” through the end is not from the words of the Prophet ﷺ. Rather, it is from the words of Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh may Allah be pleased with them, as explicitly stated in the narration of Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (3/774). Some scholars held that it is instead from the words of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ.
The word khulāsī refers to a brownish complexion. A boy may be described as khulāsī when his complexion is between white and black.

أمرني رسول الله ﷺ فتعلمت له كتاب يهود، وقال:
«إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ مَا آمَنُ يَهُودَ عَلَى كِتَابِي».
فتعلمته، فلم يمر إلا نصف شهر حتى حذقته، فكنت أكتب له إذا كتب، وأقرأ له إذا كُتب إليه.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٤٥)، والترمذي (٢٧١٥)، وصححه الحاكم (١/٧٥).
ورواه الإمام أحمد (٢١٥٨٧)، وفيه قال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
«تُحْسِنُ السُّرْيَانِيَّةَ؟ إِنَّهَا تَأْتِينِي كُتُبٌ».
قال: قلت: لا.
قال:
«فَتَعَلَّمْهَا».
فتعلمتها في سبعة عشر يومًا.

1186 — Zayd ibn Thābit may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed me to learn the writing of the Jews for him, and he said:
“By Allah, I do not trust the Jews concerning my correspondence.”
So I learned it. Less than half a month passed before I had mastered it. Thereafter, I would write for him when he wished to send correspondence, and I would read for him when letters were sent to him.
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3645) and al-Tirmidhī (2715), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (1/75).
Imām Aḥmad also narrated it (21587). In that wording, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“Do you know Syriac? Letters come to me in that language.”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
“Then learn it.”
So I learned it in seventeen days.

١١٨٨ — عن زيد بن أرقم رضي الله عنه قال:
لا أقول لكم إلا كما كان رسول الله ﷺ يقول. كان يقول:
«اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَالْهَرَمِ وَعَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ. اللَّهُمَّ آتِ نَفْسِي تَقْوَاهَا، وَزَكِّهَا أَنْتَ خَيْرُ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا، أَنْتَ وَلِيُّهَا وَمَوْلَاهَا. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لَا يَخْشَعُ، وَمِنْ نَفْسٍ لَا تَشْبَعُ، وَمِنْ دَعْوَةٍ لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهَا».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٢٢).

1188 — Zayd ibn Arqam may Allah be pleased with him said:
I will say to you only what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say. He would say:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, cowardice and miserliness, decrepit old age, and the punishment of the grave.
O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it. You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that does not humble itself, from a soul that is never satisfied, and from a supplication that is not answered.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2722).

«اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَالْهَرَمِ وَعَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ. اللَّهُمَّ آتِ نَفْسِي تَقْوَاهَا، وَزَكِّهَا أَنْتَ خَيْرُ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا، أَنْتَ وَلِيُّهَا وَمَوْلَاهَا. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لَا يَخْشَعُ، وَمِنْ نَفْسٍ لَا تَشْبَعُ، وَمِنْ دَعْوَةٍ لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهَا».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٢٢).
1188 — Zayd ibn Arqam may Allah be pleased with him said:
I will say to you only what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say. He would say:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, cowardice and miserliness, decrepit old age, and the punishment of the grave.
O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it. You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that does not humble itself, from a soul that is never satisfied, and from a supplication that is not answered.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2722).

arabic_source:
١١٨٩ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال:
كان النبي ﷺ يتعوذ من علم لا ينفع، ودعاء لا يُسمع، وقلب لا يخشع، ونفس لا تشبع.
صحيح: رواه النسائي (٥٤٤٢)، وأحمد (٦٥٥٧)، والترمذي (٣٤٨٢)، وقال: «حسن صحيح غريب».

١١٩١ — عن مكحول أنه دخل على أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه، قال: فسمعته يذكر أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يقول:
«اللَّهُمَّ انْفَعْنِي بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنِي، وَعَلِّمْنِي مَا يَنْفَعُنِي، وَارْزُقْنِي عِلْمًا تَنْفَعُنِي بِهِ».
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الدعاء (٣/١٤٥٥، رقم ١٤٠٥)، والحاكم (١/٥١٠).

1191 — Makḥūl reported:
I entered upon Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him and heard him mention that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
“O Allah, benefit me through what You have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and provide me with knowledge through which You will benefit me.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (3/1455, no. 1405) and al-Ḥākim (1/510).

١١٩٢ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إِذَا مَاتَ الْإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَمَلُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ ثَلَاثٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٣١).

1192 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When a human being dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: an ongoing charity, knowledge from which people benefit, or a righteous child who supplicates for him.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (1631).

١١٩٣ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ مِمَّا يَلْحَقُ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ وَحَسَنَاتِهِ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ: عِلْمًا عَلَّمَهُ وَنَشَرَهُ، وَوَلَدًا صَالِحًا تَرَكَهُ، وَمُصْحَفًا وَرَّثَهُ، أَوْ مَسْجِدًا بَنَاهُ، أَوْ بَيْتًا لِابْنِ السَّبِيلِ بَنَاهُ، أَوْ نَهْرًا أَجْرَاهُ، أَوْ صَدَقَةً أَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ مَالِهِ فِي صِحَّتِهِ وَحَيَاتِهِ، يَلْحَقُهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ».
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٤٢).

english_source:
1193 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the deeds and good works whose reward continues to reach a believer after his death are: knowledge that he taught and spread; a righteous child whom he left behind; a copy of the Qurʾān that he bequeathed; a mosque that he built; a house that he built for a traveler; a river that he caused to flow; or charity that he gave from his wealth during his health and lifetime. These continue to reach him after his death.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (242).

«إِنَّ مِمَّا يَلْحَقُ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ وَحَسَنَاتِهِ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ: عِلْمًا عَلَّمَهُ وَنَشَرَهُ، وَوَلَدًا صَالِحًا تَرَكَهُ، وَمُصْحَفًا وَرَّثَهُ، أَوْ مَسْجِدًا بَنَاهُ، أَوْ بَيْتًا لِابْنِ السَّبِيلِ بَنَاهُ، أَوْ نَهْرًا أَجْرَاهُ، أَوْ صَدَقَةً أَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ مَالِهِ فِي صِحَّتِهِ وَحَيَاتِهِ، يَلْحَقُهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ».

١١٩٥ — عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أَقِيلُوا ذَوِي الْهَيْئَاتِ عَثَرَاتِهِمْ إِلَّا الْحُدُودَ».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٣٧٥).
وقوله: «أقيلوا ذوي الهيئات عثراتهم»؛ أي سامحوا الصالحين من ذوي الهيئات الحسنة من أخطائهم وسيئاتهم، وذوو الهيئات هم أهل العلم والدين.
والعثرات قيل: الصغائر، والاستثناء بقوله: «إلا الحدود» منقطع. وقيل: الذنوب مطلقًا، والمراد بالحدود ما يوجبها من الذنوب، والاستثناء متصل، والخطاب مع الأئمة وغيرهم ممن يستحق المؤاخذة والتأديب عليها.
وقد جاء في الصحيحين، البخاري (٣٧٩٩)، ومسلم (٢٥١٠)، عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ في فضل الأنصار:
«الْأَنْصَارُ كَرِشِي وَعَيْبَتِي، وَالنَّاسُ سَيَكْثُرُونَ وَيَقِلُّونَ، فَاقْبَلُوا مِنْ مُحْسِنِهِمْ وَتَجَاوَزُوا عَنْ مُسِيئِهِمْ».
هذا لفظ البخاري، ولفظ مسلم:
«وَاعْفُوا عَنْ مُسِيئِهِمْ».
وقوله: «كرشي»؛ أي بطانتي وخاصتي. قال القزاز: ضُرب المثل بالكرش؛ لأنه مستقر غذاء الحيوان الذي يكون فيه نماؤه، ويقال: لفلان كرش منثورة، أي عيال كثيرة.
والعيبة، بفتح العين المهملة وسكون الياء المثناة بعدها موحدة: ما يحرز فيه الرجل نفيس ما عنده، يريد أنهم موضع سره وأمانته. قال ابن دريد: هذا من كلامه ﷺ الموجز الذي لم يسبق إليه.

1195 — ʿĀʾishah may Allah be pleased with her reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Overlook the slips of people of upright standing, except in matters requiring prescribed legal punishments.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4375).
The statement, “Overlook the slips of people of upright standing,” means: pardon righteous people of good standing for their mistakes and lapses. “People of upright standing” refers to people of knowledge and religion.
It has been said that “slips” refers specifically to minor sins, in which case the exception “except the prescribed punishments” is a disconnected exception. It has also been said that it refers to sins generally, while “the prescribed punishments” means those sins that require such punishments; according to this interpretation, the exception is connected. The instruction is directed to rulers and others who possess legitimate authority to hold people accountable and discipline them.
It is also reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections—al-Bukhārī (3799) and Muslim (2510)—from Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the virtue of the Anṣār:
“The Anṣār are my inner circle and the repository of my trust. The people will increase in number while they will decrease, so accept the good of their righteous ones and overlook the wrongs of those among them who err.”
This is the wording of al-Bukhārī. Muslim’s wording is:
“And pardon those among them who do wrong.”
The expression “my karish” means: my close inner circle and special people. Al-Qazzāz said that the belly was used as a metaphor because it is the place in which an animal’s food settles and from which its growth is sustained. It is also said, “So-and-so has a scattered belly,” meaning that he has many dependents.
The word al-ʿaybah refers to a container in which a person safeguards his most precious possessions. The meaning is that the Anṣār were the repositories of his secrets and trust.
Ibn Durayd said:
“This is among the Prophet’s ﷺ concise expressions which no one was known to have used before him.”
See Fatḥ al-Bārī (7/121).

«مَا اجْتَمَعَ قَوْمٌ فِي بَيْتٍ مِنْ بُيُوتِ اللَّهِ، يَتْلُونَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ، وَيَتَدَارَسُونَهُ بَيْنَهُمْ، إِلَّا نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّكِينَةُ، وَغَشِيَتْهُمُ الرَّحْمَةُ، وَحَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ، وَذَكَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِيمَنْ عِنْدَهُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٩٩).

arabic_source:
١١٩٧ — عن ابن بريدة أن معاوية رضي الله عنه خرج من حمص، فقال لغلامه: ائتني — يعني بثوبيه — فلبسهما، ثم دخل مسجد حمص، فركع ركعتين.
فلما فرغ إذا هو بناس جلوس، فقال لهم:
ما أجلسكم؟
قالوا: صلينا صلاة المكتوبة، ثم قص القاص، فلما فرغ قعدنا نتذاكر سنة النبي ﷺ.
فقال معاوية رضي الله عنه:
ما من رجل أدرك النبي ﷺ أقل حديثًا عنه مني، إني سأحدثكم بخصلتين حفظتهما عن رسول الله ﷺ:
«مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ عَلَى النَّاسِ، فَيَقُومُ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ الرِّجَالُ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَكْثُرَ الْخُصُومُ عِنْدَهُ، فَدَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ».
قال:
وكنت مع النبي ﷺ يومًا، فدخل المسجد، فإذا هو بقوم في المسجد قعود، فقال النبي ﷺ:
«مَا يُقْعِدُكُمْ؟»
قالوا:
صلينا صلاة المكتوبة، ثم قعدنا نتذاكر كتاب الله وسنة نبيه.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ شَيْئًا تَعَاظَمَ ذِكْرُهُ».
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (١/٩٤)، وعنه البيهقي في المدخل (٤١٨).

1197 — Ibn Buraydah reported:
Muʿāwiyah may Allah be pleased with him came out from Ḥimṣ and said to his servant, “Bring them to me,” meaning his two garments. He put them on, then entered the mosque of Ḥimṣ and prayed two rakʿahs.
When he finished, he found some people sitting and asked them:
“What has caused you to remain seated?”
They replied:
“We prayed the obligatory prayer, then the preacher delivered an exhortation. When he finished, we remained sitting and began discussing the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.”
Muʿāwiyah may Allah be pleased with him said:
“No man who met the Prophet ﷺ narrated fewer ḥadīths from him than I did. I will narrate to you two matters that I preserved from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
‘No man who is placed in authority over people, with men standing over him, and who loves having many disputants gathered before him will enter Paradise.’”
He continued:
“One day I was with the Prophet ﷺ. He entered the mosque and found a group sitting there. The Prophet ﷺ asked:
‘What has caused you to remain seated?’
They replied:
‘We prayed the obligatory prayer, then remained sitting to discuss the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
‘Indeed, when Allah is mentioned concerning something, His mention magnifies it.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (1/94), and from him by al-Bayhaqī in al-Madkhal (418).

«لَا يَقُصُّ عَلَى النَّاسِ إِلَّا أَمِيرٌ، أَوْ مَأْمُورٌ، أَوْ مُرَاءٍ».

1198 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“No one should give public exhortation to the people except a ruler, one who has been authorized to do so, or a person seeking to show off and argue.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (3753).

١١٩٩ — عن عوف بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«لَا يَقُصُّ إِلَّا أَمِيرٌ، أَوْ مَأْمُورٌ، أَوْ مُخْتَالٌ».

I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No one should give public exhortation except a ruler, one who has been authorized to do so, or an arrogant person.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3665).

١٢٠١ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال:
لم يقص في زمن النبي ﷺ، ولا أبي بكر، ولا عمر، ولا عثمان، إنما كان القصص في زمن الفتنة.
صحيح: رواه ابن حبان (٦٢٦١)، والسياق له، وابن أبي شيبة (٢٦٧١٤)، ورواه ابن ماجه (٣٧٥٤).
وقوله: «يقص»؛ أي يعظ ويعلم. وفيه من الفوائد العظيمة أن الوعظ والتعليم في المساجد أو في الأماكن العامة يكون مرتبطًا بإذن السلطان، خوفًا من نشر الفتن والأفكار الضالة في المجتمع الإسلامي، فللجهة المخولة من السلطان أن تراقب كل من يخالف هذه القاعدة، وتمنعه من الوعظ في الأماكن المذكورة.

english_source:
1201 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them said:
“Public exhortation by storytellers was not practiced during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, nor during the time of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, or ʿUthmān. Rather, this form of public storytelling arose during the time of tribulation.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6261), whose wording is cited here, Ibn Abī Shaybah (26714), and Ibn Mājah (3754).
The expression “he gives qaṣaṣ” means that he gives admonition and instruction. Among the important lessons derived from this is that public preaching and teaching in mosques or other public places should be connected to authorization from the legitimate authority, out of concern that tribulations and deviant ideas may be spread within the Muslim community. Accordingly, the authority delegated by the ruler may supervise those who violate this rule and prevent them from giving public exhortation in such places.

١٢٠٢ — عن أبي حميد وأبي أسيد رضي الله عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال:
«إِذَا سَمِعْتُمُ الْحَدِيثَ عَنِّي تَعْرِفُهُ قُلُوبُكُمْ، وَتَلِينُ لَهُ أَشْعَارُكُمْ وَأَبْشَارُكُمْ، وَتَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُ مِنْكُمْ قَرِيبٌ، فَأَنَا أَوْلَاكُمْ بِهِ. وَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمُ الْحَدِيثَ عَنِّي تُنْكِرُهُ قُلُوبُكُمْ، وَتَنْفِرُ أَشْعَارُكُمْ وَأَبْشَارُكُمْ، وَتَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُ مِنْكُمْ بَعِيدٌ، فَأَنَا أَبْعَدُكُمْ مِنْهُ».
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٦٠٥٨)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (١٨٧)، وصححه ابن حبان (٦٣).

1202 — Abū Ḥumayd and Abū Usayd may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When you hear a ḥadīth attributed to me which your hearts recognize, toward which your hair and skin become receptive, and which you perceive to be close to you, then I am the most entitled to such a report.
But when you hear a ḥadīth attributed to me which your hearts reject, from which your hair and skin recoil, and which you perceive to be far from you, then I am the farthest of you from such a report.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (16058) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (187), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (63).

«النَّاسُ مَعَادِنُ، خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ إِذَا فَقِهُوا، وَتَجِدُونَ مِنْ خَيْرِ النَّاسِ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ كَرَاهِيَةً لِهَذَا الشَّأْنِ حَتَّى يَقَعَ فِيهِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٩٦)، ومسلم (٢٥٢٦).

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3496) and Muslim (2526).

١٢٠٥ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قيل:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، من أكرم الناس؟
قال:
«أَتْقَاهُمْ».
قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك.
قال:
«فَيُوسُفُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ، ابْنُ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ، ابْنِ خَلِيلِ اللَّهِ».
قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك.
قال:
«فَعَنْ مَعَادِنِ الْعَرَبِ تَسْأَلُونَ؟ خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ إِذَا فَقِهُوا».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٥٣)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٨)، ولفظهما سواء.

1205 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
It was asked:
“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who are the noblest of people?”
He replied:
“Those who have the most taqwā.”
They said:
“That is not what we are asking about.”
He said:
“Then Yūsuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of a Prophet of Allah, son of the intimate friend of Allah.”
They said:
“That is not what we are asking about.”
He said:
“Then are you asking about the ancestral stocks of the Arabs? The best of them in the pre-Islamic era are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding of the religion.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3353) and Muslim (2378), and their wording is the same.

١٢٠٧ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لَيْسَ الْخَبَرُ كَالْمُعَايَنَةِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَخْبَرَ مُوسَى بِمَا صَنَعَ قَوْمُهُ فِي الْعِجْلِ، فَلَمْ يُلْقِ الْأَلْوَاحَ، فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ مَا صَنَعُوا أَلْقَى الْأَلْوَاحَ فَانْكَسَرَتْ».
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٤٤٧)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٢٥)، وفي الكبير (١١٨٣، ١١٨٤)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٢٠٠).

1207 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Being informed is not like seeing directly. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed Mūsā of what his people had done with the calf, yet he did not cast down the Tablets. But when he saw directly what they had done, he cast down the Tablets and they broke.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (2447), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (25) and al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (1183, 1184), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (200).

١٢٠٨ — عن حميد بن أبي حميد الطويل قال: كنا مع أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه فقال:
والله ما كل ما نحدثكم عن رسول الله ﷺ سمعناه منه، ولكن لم يكن يكذب بعضنا بعضًا.
حسن: رواه الطبراني (٦٩٩).

1208 — Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl reported:
We were with Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him, and he said:
“By Allah, not everything we narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did we hear directly from him. Rather, we narrated from one another, and none of us used to lie to another.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī (699).

١٢١٠ — عن شداد بن أوس رضي الله عنه قال:
كان أبو ذر رضي الله عنه يسمع الحديث من رسول الله ﷺ فيه الشدة، ثم يخرج إلى قومه يسلم عليهم، ثم إن رسول الله ﷺ يرخص فيه بعد، فلم يسمعه أبو ذر، فيتعلق أبو ذر بالأمر الشديد.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧١٣٧)، والطبراني (٧١٦٦).

1210 — Shaddād ibn Aws may Allah be pleased with him reported:
Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him would sometimes hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a ḥadīth containing strictness. Then he would go out to his people and greet them. Later, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would grant a concession concerning that matter, but Abū Dharr would not hear it, so he would continue adhering to the earlier, stricter ruling.
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (17137) and al-Ṭabarānī (7166).

arabic_source:
١٢١١ — عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه قال:
قام فينا رسول الله ﷺ مقامًا، ما ترك شيئًا يكون في مقامه ذلك إلى قيام الساعة إلا حدث به؛ حفظه من حفظه، ونسيه من نسيه، قد علمه أصحابه هؤلاء. وإنه ليكون منه الشيء قد نسيته، فأراه فأذكره، كما يذكر الرجل وجه الرجل إذا غاب عنه، ثم إذا رآه عرفه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٦٠٤)، ومسلم (٢٨٩١).
وهذا لفظ مسلم، ولفظ البخاري نحوه.
وفي لفظ لمسلم:
«أَخْبَرَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ إِلَى قِيَامِ السَّاعَةِ، فَمَا مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ إِلَّا قَدْ سَأَلْتُهُ، إِلَّا أَنِّي لَمْ أَسْأَلْهُ مَا يُخْرِجُ أَهْلَ الْمَدِينَةِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ».
وروى البزار في كشف الأستار (١٤٨):
«عُرِضَتْ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ أُمَّتُهُ، فَقُمْتُ خَلْفَهُ، فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ، فَقَالَ: كُنْتَ هَاهُنَا؟ هَلْ سَمِعْتَ؟ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ».
وكان حذيفة يقول:
هل في هذا ما حفظ رجل؟
قال: فقام فينا فأخبرنا بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، أو قال: فأخبرنا بما بيننا وبين الساعة؛ حفظه من حفظه، ونسيه من نسيه.

english_source:
1211 — Ḥudhayfah may Allah be pleased with him said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood before us on one occasion and did not leave out anything that would occur from that time until the establishment of the Hour except that he informed us of it. Whoever retained it retained it, and whoever forgot it forgot it. These Companions of his knew it.
Sometimes an event from among those matters would occur after I had forgotten it, then when I saw it I would remember it, just as a man remembers the face of another man who has been absent from him and then recognizes him when he sees him again.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6604) and Muslim (2891).
This is Muslim’s wording, while al-Bukhārī’s wording is similar.
In another wording in Muslim:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me of everything that would occur until the establishment of the Hour. There was nothing among those matters except that I asked him about it, except that I did not ask him what would drive the people of Madinah out of Madinah.”
Al-Bazzār narrated in Kashf al-Astār (148):
“The Ummah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was presented before him, and I stood behind him. When he had finished, he turned toward me and asked, ‘Were you here? Did you hear?’
I replied, ‘Yes.’”
Ḥudhayfah used to say:
“Could any person fully retain all of this?”
He said:
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and informed us of what would occur until the Day of Resurrection—or he said: he informed us of everything between us and the Hour. Whoever retained it retained it, and whoever forgot it forgot it.

١٢١٢ — عن عمرو بن أخطب رضي الله عنه قال:
صلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ الفجر، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى حضرت الظهر، فنزل فصلى، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى حضرت العصر، ثم نزل فصلى، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى غربت الشمس، فأخبرنا بما كان وبما هو كائن، فأعلمنا أحفظنا.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨٩٢).

١٢١٢ — عن عمرو بن أخطب رضي الله عنه قال:
صلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ الفجر، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى حضرت الظهر، فنزل فصلى، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى حضرت العصر، ثم نزل فصلى، ثم صعد المنبر فخطبنا حتى غربت الشمس، فأخبرنا بما كان وبما هو كائن، فأعلمنا أحفظنا.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨٩٢).
english_source:
1212 — ʿAmr ibn Akhṭab may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the Fajr prayer, then ascended the pulpit and addressed us until the time for Ẓuhr arrived.
He descended and prayed, then ascended the pulpit again and addressed us until the time for ʿAṣr arrived.
He descended and prayed, then ascended the pulpit again and addressed us until the sun set.
He informed us of what had already occurred and what would occur in the future. The most knowledgeable among us concerning those matters was the one who remembered the most.
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2892).

١٢١٣ — عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال:
تركنا رسول الله ﷺ وما طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا عندنا منه علم.
صحيح: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٤٧)، والطبراني (١٦٤٧).
وزاد فيه:
«مَا بَقِيَ شَيْءٌ يُقَرِّبُ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَيُبَاعِدُ مِنَ النَّارِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ بُيِّنَ لَكُمْ».
وصححه ابن حبان (٦٥).
وقوله: «إلا عندنا منه علم»، قال ابن حبان:
«يعني أوامره ونواهيه، وأخباره وأفعاله وإباحته».

english_source:
1213 — Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left us, and there was not even a bird flying with its two wings except that we had been given some knowledge concerning it.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (147) and al-Ṭabarānī (1647).
An additional wording states:
“Nothing remains that brings one closer to Paradise and distances one from the Fire except that it has already been made clear to you.”
Ibn Ḥibbān authenticated it (65).
Regarding the statement, “except that we had knowledge concerning it,” Ibn Ḥibbān said:
“That is, knowledge of his commands and prohibitions, his reports, his actions, and what he permitted.”

١٢١٤ — عن أبي برزة الأسلمي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمَا عَبْدٍ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ عُمُرِهِ فِيمَا أَفْنَاهُ، وَعَنْ عِلْمِهِ فِيمَا فَعَلَ، وَعَنْ مَالِهِ مِنْ أَيْنَ اكْتَسَبَهُ وَفِيمَا أَنْفَقَهُ، وَعَنْ جِسْمِهِ فِيمَا أَبْلَاهُ».
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٤١٧)، وقال: «هذا حديث حسن صحيح».

1214 — Abū Barzah al-Aslamī may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about his life and how he spent it, about his knowledge and what he did with it, about his wealth—where he acquired it and how he spent it—and about his body and how he wore it out.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2417), who said: “This ḥadīth is Ḥasan Ṣaḥīḥ.”

١٢١٦ — عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ كَانَتْ عِنْدَهُ وَلِيدَةٌ فَعَلَّمَهَا فَأَحْسَنَ تَعْلِيمَهَا، وَأَدَّبَهَا فَأَحْسَنَ تَأْدِيبَهَا، ثُمَّ أَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا فَلَهُ أَجْرَانِ. وَأَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ آمَنَ بِنَبِيِّهِ وَآمَنَ بِي فَلَهُ أَجْرَانِ. وَأَيُّمَا مَمْلُوكٍ أَدَّى حَقَّ مَوَالِيهِ وَحَقَّ رَبِّهِ فَلَهُ أَجْرَانِ».
وقال الشعبي:
خذها بغير شيء، وقد كان الرجل يرحل فيما دونه إلى المدينة.
وقال أبو بكر، عن أبي حصين، عن أبي بردة، عن أبيه، عن النبي ﷺ:
«أَعْتَقَهَا ثُمَّ أَصْدَقَهَا».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٨٣)، ومسلم (١٥٤)، واللفظ للبخاري.

١٢١٧ — عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«هَلَاكُ أُمَّتِي فِي الْكِتَابِ وَاللَّبَنِ».
قالوا:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، ما الكتاب واللبن؟
قال:
«يَتَعَلَّمُونَ الْقُرْآنَ فَيَتَأَوَّلُونَهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ، وَيُحِبُّونَ اللَّبَنَ فَيَدَعُونَ الْجَمَاعَاتِ وَالْجُمَعَ وَيَبْدُونَ».
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٤١٥)، وأبو يعلى في المقصد العلي (٣٦٩).

1217 — ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“The destruction of my Ummah will be through the Book and milk.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what are the Book and milk?”
He replied:
“They will learn the Qurʾān and interpret it in a manner other than that in which Allah revealed it. And they will love milk, so they will abandon the congregational prayers and Friday prayers and go out to live in the desert.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (17415) and Abū Yaʿlā in al-Maqṣad al-ʿAlī (369).

«يَكُونُ خَلْفٌ مِنْ بَعْدِ سِتِّينَ سَنَةً أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ خَلْفٌ يَقْرَؤُونَ الْقُرْآنَ لَا يَعْدُو تَرَاقِيَهُمْ، وَيَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ ثَلَاثَةٌ: مُؤْمِنٌ، وَمُنَافِقٌ، وَفَاجِرٌ».
قال بشير:
فقلت للوليد: ما هؤلاء الثلاثة؟
فقال:
المنافق كافر به، والفاجر يتأكل به، والمؤمن يؤمن به.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١١٣٤٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧٥٥)، والحاكم (٢/٧٤).

1218 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“There will come a later generation after sixty years who will neglect the prayer and follow their desires, so they will soon encounter ruin.
Then there will come another generation who recite the Qurʾān, but it will not pass beyond their collarbones.
Three types of people recite the Qurʾān: a believer, a hypocrite, and an immoral sinner.”
Bashīr said:
I asked al-Walīd:
“Who are these three?”
He replied:
“The hypocrite disbelieves in it, the immoral sinner uses it as a means of earning worldly benefit, and the believer truly believes in it.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (11340), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (755) and al-Ḥākim (2/74).

I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“There will come a later generation after sixty years who will neglect the prayer and follow their desires, so they will soon encounter ruin.
Then there will come another generation who recite the Qurʾān, but it will not pass beyond their collarbones.
Three types of people recite the Qurʾān: a believer, a hypocrite, and an immoral sinner.”
Bashīr said:
I asked al-Walīd:
“Who are these three?”
He replied:
“The hypocrite disbelieves in it, the immoral sinner uses it as a means of earning worldly benefit, and the believer truly believes in it.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (11340), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (755) and al-Ḥākim (2/74).

١٢٢١ — عن سعيد بن عمرو بن العاص قال:
كنت عند ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، فأتاه رجل فقال: من أنت؟
فمنَّ له برحم بعيدة، فألان له القول، فقال:
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«اعْرِفُوا أَنْسَابَكُمْ تَصِلُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَا قُرْبَ بِالرَّحِمِ إِذَا قُطِعَتْ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ قَرِيبَةً، وَلَا بُعْدَ بِهَا إِذَا وُصِلَتْ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ بَعِيدَةً».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (٢٨٨٠).

english_source:
1221 — Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ reported:
I was with Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them when a man came to him. Ibn ʿAbbās asked:
“Who are you?”
The man mentioned a distant family connection between them, so Ibn ʿAbbās spoke gently to him and then said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Know your genealogies so that you may maintain your ties of kinship. There is no true closeness through kinship when it is severed, even if the blood relationship is near; and there is no true distance when it is maintained, even if the blood relationship is distant.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī (2880).

قدم رجلان من المشرق فخطبا، فعجب الناس لبيانهما، فقال النبي ﷺ:
«إِنَّ مِنَ الْبَيَانِ لَسِحْرًا».
أو قال:
«إِنَّ بَعْضَ الْبَيَانِ لَسِحْرٌ».
صحيح: رواه مالك (٧)، والبخاري (٥٧٦٧).

Two men came from the East and delivered speeches, and the people were impressed by their eloquence.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Indeed, some eloquent speech is like magic.”
Or he said:
“Indeed, some forms of eloquent speech are like magic.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Mālik (7) and al-Bukhārī (5767).

Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5011), al-Tirmidhī (2845), and Ibn Mājah (3756).

«إِنَّ مِنَ الْبَيَانِ سِحْرًا، وَإِنَّ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ حِكَمًا».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠١١)، والترمذي (٢٨٤٥)، وابن ماجه (٣٧٥٦).
1223 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported:
A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and began speaking eloquently. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, some eloquent speech is like magic, and indeed some poetry contains wisdom.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5011), al-Tirmidhī (2845), and Ibn Mājah (3756).

١٢٢٥ — عن أبي أمية الجمحي رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إِنَّ مِنْ أَشْرَاطِ السَّاعَةِ ثَلَاثًا، إِحْدَاهُنَّ أَنْ يُلْتَمَسَ الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ الْأَصَاغِرِ».
حسن: رواه الطبراني (٢٢/٣٦١–٣٦٢)، وابن عبد البر في جامع بيان العلم (١٠٥٢).

١٢٢٦ — عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن النبي ﷺ كان يجمع بين الرجلين من قتلى أُحد — يعني في القبر — ثم يقول:
«أَيُّهُمَا أَكْثَرُ أَخْذًا لِلْقُرْآنِ؟»
فإذا أُشير إلى أحدهما قدَّمه في اللحد.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٣٤٣).

english_source:
1226 — Jābir may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Prophet ﷺ used to place two of the martyrs of Uḥud together in one grave, then ask:
“Which of the two had learned more of the Qurʾān?”
When one of them was indicated, he would place him first in the niche of the grave.
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1343).

١٢٢٧ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ مِنْ إِجْلَالِ اللَّهِ إِكْرَامَ ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ الْمُسْلِمِ، وَحَامِلِ الْقُرْآنِ غَيْرِ الْغَالِي فِيهِ وَالْجَافِي عَنْهُ، وَإِكْرَامَ ذِي السُّلْطَانِ الْمُقْسِطِ».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٨٤٣).

١٢٢٨ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال:
لما نزلت بنو قريظة على حكم سعد رضي الله عنه، بعث رسول الله ﷺ إليه، وكان قريبًا، فجاء على حمار، فلما دنا قال النبي ﷺ:
«قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٤٣)، ومسلم (١٧٦٨).
قال مسلم بن الحجاج:
«لا أعلم في قيام الرجل للرجل حديثًا أصح من هذا، وهذا القيام على وجه البر لا على وجه التعظيم، أمر النبي ﷺ الأنصار أن يقوموا إلى سيدهم».
رواه البيهقي في المدخل (٧٠٨) بإسناده إلى مسلم بن الحجاج.
وقال الخطابي في معالم السنن (٥/٣٩٠):
«إن قيام المرء بين يدي الرئيس الفاضل، والوالي العادل، وقيام المتعلم للعالم مستحب غير مكروه، وإنما جاءت الكراهية فيمن كان بخلاف أهل هذه الصفات».

1228 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
When Banū Qurayẓah agreed to accept the judgment of Saʿd may Allah be pleased with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him. He was nearby and came riding upon a donkey.
When he drew near, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Stand up for your leader.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3043) and Muslim (1768).
Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj said:
“I do not know of any ḥadīth concerning a man standing for another man that is more authentic than this one. This standing was by way of kindness and respect, not by way of excessive glorification. The Prophet ﷺ commanded the Anṣār to stand for their leader.”
Narrated by al-Bayhaqī in al-Madkhal (708) with his chain to Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj.
Al-Khaṭṭābī said in Maʿālim al-Sunan (5/390):
“A person standing before a virtuous leader or a just governor, and a student standing for a scholar, is recommended and not disliked. The prohibition or dislike applies to those who do not possess such qualities.”

١٢٢٨ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال:
لما نزلت بنو قريظة على حكم سعد رضي الله عنه، بعث رسول الله ﷺ إليه، وكان قريبًا، فجاء على حمار، فلما دنا قال النبي ﷺ:
«قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٤٣)، ومسلم (١٧٦٨).
قال مسلم بن الحجاج:
«لا أعلم في قيام الرجل للرجل حديثًا أصح من هذا، وهذا القيام على وجه البر لا على وجه التعظيم، أمر النبي ﷺ الأنصار أن يقوموا إلى سيدهم».
رواه البيهقي في المدخل (٧٠٨) بإسناده إلى مسلم بن الحجاج.
وقال الخطابي في معالم السنن (٥/٣٩٠):
«إن قيام المرء بين يدي الرئيس الفاضل، والوالي العادل، وقيام المتعلم للعالم مستحب غير مكروه، وإنما جاءت الكراهية فيمن كان بخلاف أهل هذه الصفات».

When Banū Qurayẓah agreed to accept the judgment of Saʿd may Allah be pleased with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him. He was nearby and came riding upon a donkey.
When he drew near, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Stand up for your leader.”

١٢٢٩ — عن كعب بن مالك رضي الله عنه، في حديث تخلفه عن رسول الله ﷺ في غزوة تبوك، قال فيه:
لما بُشرت بالتوبة انطلقت إلى رسول الله ﷺ، فتلقاني الناس فوجًا فوجًا يهنئونني بالتوبة، يقولون:
لتهنك توبة الله عليك.
حتى دخلت المسجد، فقام إليَّ طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه يهرول، حتى صافحني وهنأني، وما قام إليَّ رجل من المهاجرين غيره، ولا أنساها لطلحة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٤١٨)، ومسلم (٢٧٦٩).

1229 — Kaʿb ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him, while relating the account of his remaining behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabūk, said:
When I was given the glad tidings that my repentance had been accepted, I set out for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The people met me group after group, congratulating me upon my repentance and saying:
“May Allah’s acceptance of your repentance bring you joy.”
When I entered the mosque, Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh may Allah be pleased with him stood and hurried toward me until he shook my hand and congratulated me.
No other man among the Muhājirūn stood for me besides him, and I never forgot that gesture from Ṭalḥah.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4418) and Muslim (2769).

١٢٣٠ — عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها قالت:
ما رأيت أحدًا أشبه سمتًا ودلًّا وهديًا برسول الله ﷺ في قيامها وقعودها من فاطمة بنت رسول الله ﷺ.
قالت:
وكانت إذا دخلت على النبي ﷺ قام إليها فقبّلها وأجلسها في مجلسه، وكان النبي ﷺ إذا دخل عليها قامت من مجلسها فقبّلته وأجلسته في مجلسها.
فلما مرض النبي ﷺ دخلت فاطمة، فأكبت عليه فقبلته، ثم رفعت رأسها فبكت، ثم أكبت عليه، ثم رفعت رأسها فضحكت.
فقلت:
إن كنت لأظن أن هذه من أعقل نسائنا، فإذا هي من النساء!
فلما توفي النبي ﷺ قلت لها:
أرأيت حين أكببت على النبي ﷺ فرفعت رأسك فبكيت، ثم أكببت عليه فرفعت رأسك فضحكت، ما حملك على ذلك؟
قالت:
إني حين أكببت عليه أخبرني أنه ميت من وجعه هذا، فبكيت، ثم أخبرني أني أسرع أهله لحوقًا به، فذاك حين ضحكت.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٢١٧)، والترمذي (٣٨٧٢)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٩٤٧)، والنسائي في الكبرى (٨٣١١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٦٩٥٣)، والحاكم (٤/٢٧٢–٢٧٣).

1230 — ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers may Allah be pleased with her, said:
“I never saw anyone whose manner, bearing, and conduct in standing and sitting more closely resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Whenever she entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, he would stand for her, kiss her, and seat her in his place. And whenever the Prophet ﷺ entered upon her, she would rise from her seat, kiss him, and seat him in her place.
When the Prophet ﷺ became ill, Fāṭimah entered and leaned over him and kissed him. She then raised her head and cried. Then she leaned over him again, raised her head, and laughed.
I said to myself:
‘I used to think that she was among the most intelligent of our women, but here she is behaving like other women!’
After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, I asked her:
‘When you leaned over the Prophet ﷺ and then raised your head and cried, and afterward leaned over him again, raised your head, and laughed—what caused you to do that?’
She replied:
‘When I leaned over him the first time, he informed me that he would die from this illness, so I cried. Then he informed me that I would be the first of his family to join him, and that was when I laughed.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5217), al-Tirmidhī (3872), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (947), and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8311). It was authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6953) and al-Ḥākim (4/272–273).

١٢٣١ — عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال:
اشتكى رسول الله ﷺ، فصلينا وراءه وهو قاعد، وأبو بكر رضي الله عنه يُسمع الناس تكبيره.
فالتفت إلينا فرآنا قيامًا، فأشار إلينا فقعدنا، فصلينا بصلاته قعودًا.
فلما سلّم قال:

١٢٣٢ — عن معاوية رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَتَمَثَّلَ لَهُ الرِّجَالُ قِيَامًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٢٢٩)، والترمذي (٢٧٥٥).

1232 — Muʿāwiyah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Whoever loves that men should stand before him in attendance, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5229) and al-Tirmidhī (2755).

١٢٣٣ — عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال:
ما كان شخص أحب إليهم من رسول الله ﷺ، وكانوا إذا رأوه لم يقوموا؛ لما يعلمون من كراهيته لذلك.
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢٧٥٤)، وأحمد (١٢٣٤٥)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٩٤٦)، وأبو يعلى (٣٧٨٤).

“No person was more beloved to them than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, yet when they saw him they would not stand up for him, because they knew that he disliked that.”

١٢٣٤ — عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مِنْ أَشْرَاطِ السَّاعَةِ أَنْ يَقِلَّ الْعِلْمُ، وَيَظْهَرَ الْجَهْلُ، وَيَظْهَرَ الزِّنَا، وَتَكْثُرَ النِّسَاءُ، وَيَقِلَّ الرِّجَالُ، حَتَّى يَكُونَ لِخَمْسِينَ امْرَأَةً الْقَيِّمُ الْوَاحِدُ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٨١)، ومسلم (٢٦٧١).

english_source:
1234 — Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge will diminish, ignorance will appear, fornication will become widespread, women will become numerous, and men will become few, until one man will be responsible for fifty women.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (81) and Muslim (2671).

١٢٣٥ — عن عبد الله وأبي موسى رضي الله عنهما قالا: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّامًا يُرْفَعُ فِيهَا الْعِلْمُ، وَيَنْزِلُ فِيهَا الْجَهْلُ، وَيَكْثُرُ فِيهَا الْهَرْجُ».
والهرج: القتل.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٠٦٢)، ومسلم (٢٦٧٢).

١٢٣٦ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَقْبِضُ الْعِلْمَ انْتِزَاعًا يَنْتَزِعُهُ مِنَ النَّاسِ، وَلَكِنْ يَقْبِضُ الْعِلْمَ بِقَبْضِ الْعُلَمَاءِ، حَتَّى إِذَا لَمْ يَتْرُكْ عَالِمًا اتَّخَذَ النَّاسُ رُؤُوسًا جُهَّالًا، فَسُئِلُوا فَأَفْتَوْا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ، فَضَلُّوا وَأَضَلُّوا».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٠٠)، ومسلم (٢٦٧٣).

1236 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ may Allah be pleased with them reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it out of the people. Rather, He takes away knowledge by taking away the scholars.
When no scholar remains, people will take ignorant leaders. They will be asked questions and will give religious verdicts without knowledge, so they will go astray and lead others astray.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (100) and Muslim (2673).

١٢٣٧ — عن عروة بن الزبير قال:
قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها:
يا ابن أختي، بلغني أن عبد الله بن عمرو مار بنا إلى الحج، فالقه فسائله، فإنه قد حمل عن النبي ﷺ علمًا كثيرًا.
قال: فلقيته فسألته عن أشياء يذكرها عن رسول الله ﷺ.
قال عروة: فكان فيما ذكر أن النبي ﷺ قال:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْتَزِعُ الْعِلْمَ مِنَ النَّاسِ انْتِزَاعًا، وَلَكِنَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ فَيُرْفَعُ الْعِلْمُ مَعَهُمْ، وَيُبْقِي فِي النَّاسِ رُؤُوسًا جُهَّالًا يُفْتُونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ، فَيَضِلُّونَ وَيُضِلُّونَ».
قال عروة:
فلما حدثت عائشة بذلك أعظمت ذلك وأنكرته، وقالت:
أحدثك أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول هذا؟
قال عروة:
حتى إذا كان قابل قالت له:
إن ابن عمرو قد قدم، فالقه، ثم فاتحه حتى تسأله عن الحديث الذي ذكره لك في العلم.
قال:
فلقيته فسألته، فذكره لي نحو ما حدثني به في المرة الأولى.
قال عروة:
فلما أخبرتها بذلك قالت:
ما أحسبه إلا قد صدق، أراه لم يزد فيه شيئًا ولم ينقص.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٧٣).

1237 — ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr reported:
ʿĀʾishah may Allah be pleased with her said:
“O son of my sister, I have been informed that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr will pass by us on his way to Ḥajj. Meet him and ask him questions, for he has preserved much knowledge from the Prophet ﷺ.”
ʿUrwah said:
So I met him and asked him about matters that he narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Among what he mentioned was that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah does not remove knowledge from people by forcibly snatching it away. Rather, He takes away the scholars, so knowledge is lifted along with them. He then leaves among the people ignorant leaders who issue religious verdicts without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray.”
ʿUrwah said:
When I told ʿĀʾishah about this, she regarded the matter as serious and questioned it. She asked:
“Did he tell you that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say this?”
Then when the following year came, she said:
“Ibn ʿAmr has arrived. Meet him, begin speaking with him, and then ask him about the ḥadīth concerning knowledge that he previously narrated to you.”
So I met him and asked him, and he narrated it to me in essentially the same way as he had narrated it the first time.
When I informed ʿĀʾishah, she said:
“I think he has indeed spoken truthfully. I see that he neither added anything to it nor omitted anything from it.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2673).

١٢٣٨ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«يَتَقَارَبُ الزَّمَانُ، وَيُقْبَضُ الْعِلْمُ، وَتَظْهَرُ الْفِتَنُ، وَيُلْقَى الشُّحُّ، وَيَكْثُرُ الْهَرْجُ».
قالوا:
وما الهرج؟
قال:
«الْقَتْلُ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٨٥)، ومسلم (١٥٧).
وقد ورد تفسير قبض العلم على لسان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه عند البزار في كشف الأستار (٢٣٦)، قال:
«أَمَا إِنَّ قَبْضَ الْعِلْمِ لَيْسَ شَيْئًا يُنْزَعُ مِنْ صُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ، وَلَكِنَّهُ فَنَاءُ الْعُلَمَاءِ».

1238 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Time will draw closer together, knowledge will be taken away, tribulations will appear, miserliness will be cast into people’s hearts, and harj will become widespread.”
They asked:
“What is harj?”
He replied:
“Killing.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (85) and Muslim (157).
The meaning of “the taking away of knowledge” was also explained by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb may Allah be pleased with him in al-Bazzār’s Kashf al-Astār (236). He said:
“Indeed, the taking away of knowledge is not something that is pulled out from the chests of men. Rather, it is the passing away of the scholars.”

١٢٤٠ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«سَيَأْتِي عَلَى أُمَّتِي زَمَانٌ يَكْثُرُ الْقُرَّاءُ، وَيَقِلُّ الْفُقَهَاءُ، وَيُقْبَضُ الْعِلْمُ، وَيَكْثُرُ الْهَرْجُ».
قالوا:
وما الهرج؟
قال:
«الْقَتْلُ بَيْنَكُمْ».
ثم يأتي بعد ذلك زمان يقرأ القرآن رجال لا يجاوز تراقيهم، ثم يأتي زمان يجادل المنافق المشرك المؤمن.
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط، كما في مجمع البحرين (٢٧٣).

1240 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A time will come upon my Ummah when reciters of the Qurʾān will be numerous, while jurists and people of deep understanding will be few. Knowledge will be taken away and harj will increase.”
They asked:
“What is harj?”
He replied:
“Killing among yourselves.”
Then after that will come a time when men will recite the Qurʾān, but it will not go beyond their collarbones. Then there will come a time when the hypocrite and polytheist will argue against the believer.
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, as cited in Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (273).

«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْزِعُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْكُمْ بَعْدَمَا أَعْطَاكُمُوهُ انْتِزَاعًا، وَلَكِنْ يَقْبِضُ الْعُلَمَاءَ بِعِلْمِهِمْ، وَيَبْقَى جُهَّالٌ، فَيُسْأَلُونَ فَيُفْتُونَ، فَيَضِلُّونَ وَيُضِلُّونَ».
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط، كما في مجمع البحرين (٣٣٤).

“Allah will not take knowledge away from you after having given it to you by forcibly pulling it out. Rather, He will take away the scholars together with their knowledge.

arabic_source:
١٢٤٢ — عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ نظر إلى السماء يومًا فقال:
«هَذَا أَوَانُ يُرْفَعُ الْعِلْمُ».
فقال رجل من الأنصار يقال له لبيد بن زياد:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، يُرفع العلم وقد أُثبت ووعته القلوب؟
فقال له رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنْ كُنْتُ لَأَحْسَبُكَ مِنْ أَفْقَهِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ».
وذكر له ضلالة اليهود والنصارى على ما في أيديهم من كتاب الله.
قال: فلقيت شداد بن أوس فحدثته بحديث عوف بن مالك، فقال:
صدق عوف، ألا أخبرك بأول ذلك يُرفع؟
قلت: بلى.
قال:
الخشوع، حتى لا ترى خاشعًا.
صحيح: رواه النسائي في السنن الكبرى (٥٨٧٨).

1242 — ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked toward the sky one day and said:
“This is the time when knowledge will be lifted.”
A man from the Anṣār named Labīd ibn Ziyād asked:

١٢٤٣ — عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال:
كنا مع رسول الله ﷺ، فشخص ببصره إلى السماء، ثم قال:
«هَذَا أَوَانُ يُخْتَلَسُ الْعِلْمُ مِنَ النَّاسِ، حَتَّى لَا يَقْدِرُوا مِنْهُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ».
فقال زياد بن لبيد الأنصاري:
كيف يُختلس منا وقد قرأنا القرآن؟ فوالله لنقرأنه ولنقرئنه نساءنا وأبناءنا.
فقال:
«ثَكِلَتْكَ أُمُّكَ يَا زِيَادُ، إِنْ كُنْتُ لَأَعُدُّكَ مِنْ فُقَهَاءِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ، هَذِهِ التَّوْرَاةُ وَالْإِنْجِيلُ عِنْدَ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى، فَمَاذَا تُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ؟»
قال جبير:
فلقيت عبادة بن الصامت فقلت:
ألا تسمع إلى ما يقول أخوك أبو الدرداء؟
فأخبرته بما قال أبو الدرداء.
قال:
صدق أبو الدرداء. إن شئت لأحدثنك بأول علم يُرفع من الناس: الخشوع، يوشك أن تدخل مسجد جماعة فلا ترى فيه رجلًا خاشعًا.
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٦٥٣)، وقال: «هذا حديث حسن غريب».
قال الأعظمي: إسناده حسن.
وصححه الحاكم (١/٩٩)، وذكر وجه تصحيحه، وقال الأعظمي: «وهذا كلام جيد مقبول، مبني على قواعد أهل هذا الفن».
وروي أيضًا من حديث زياد بن لبيد عند ابن ماجه (٤٠٤٨)، وأحمد (١٧٤٧٣، ١٧٩١٩)، وأبي خيثمة (٥٢)، والحاكم (٣/٥٩٠)، إلا أن سالم بن أبي الجعد لم يسمع من زياد بن لبيد.

1243 — Abū al-Dardāʾ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he raised his gaze toward the sky and said:
“This is the time when knowledge will be snatched away from the people until they will be unable to retain anything of it.”
Ziyād ibn Labīd al-Anṣārī asked:
“How can it be snatched away from us when we have recited the Qurʾān? By Allah, we will certainly continue to recite it and teach it to our women and children.”
He said:
“May your mother lose you, O Ziyād! I used to consider you among the jurists of the people of Madinah. The Torah and the Gospel are in the possession of the Jews and Christians, yet what benefit have they brought them?”
Jubayr said:
I met ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and said:
“Do you not hear what your brother Abū al-Dardāʾ is saying?”
I then told him what Abū al-Dardāʾ had said.
He replied:
“Abū al-Dardāʾ has spoken the truth. If you wish, I will tell you the first knowledge that will be lifted from the people: khushūʿ. Soon you will enter a congregational mosque and not see a single man in it possessing khushūʿ.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2653), who said: “This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth.”
Al-Aʿẓamī said: Its chain is ḥasan.
Al-Ḥākim authenticated it (1/99) and stated the basis for his authentication. Al-Aʿẓamī said: “This is sound and acceptable reasoning, built upon the principles of the specialists in this field.”
It was also narrated from Ziyād ibn Labīd by Ibn Mājah (4048), Aḥmad (17473, 17919), Abū Khaythamah (52), and al-Ḥākim (3/590), although Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd did not hear from Ziyād ibn Labīd.

١٢٤٤ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«مَنْ أُفْتِيَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَانَ إِثْمُهُ عَلَى مَنْ أَفْتَاهُ».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٥٧)، ورواه ابن ماجه (٥٣).
ورواه أبو داود من وجه آخر بزيادة: «ومن أشار على أخيه بأمر يعلم أن الرشد في غيره فقد خانه»، وهذه الزيادة ضعيفة من أجل عمرو بن أبي نعيمة.
وذكر الأعظمي ما يتعلق باختلاف طرقه وزيادة الثقة، ثم أورد من كلام السلف في التثبت في الفتيا قول ابن عباس: «من أفتى بفتيا هو يعمي فيها كان إثمها عليه»، وقول ابن مسعود فيمن كان عنده علم أن يقوله، ومن لم يكن عنده علم أن يقول: الله أعلم.

1244 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever is given a religious verdict without knowledge, its sin is upon the one who gave him that verdict.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3657) and Ibn Mājah (53).
Abū Dāwūd also narrated it through another route with the addition: “Whoever advises his brother to do something while knowing that right guidance lies elsewhere has betrayed him.” This addition is weak because of ʿAmr ibn Abī Nuʿaymah.
Al-Aʿẓamī discussed the differing routes and the issue of an additional narrator in a connected chain, then cited statements of the early Muslims concerning caution in issuing religious verdicts, including the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās: “Whoever gives a verdict concerning a matter while being blind to it bears its sin,” and the statement of Ibn Masʿūd that whoever possesses knowledge should speak, and whoever does not should say: Allah knows best.

١٢٤٥ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدّه، قال: سمع النبي ﷺ قومًا يتدارؤون، فقال:
«إِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ بِهَذَا، ضَرَبُوا كِتَابَ اللَّهِ بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ، وَإِنَّمَا نَزَلَ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ يُصَدِّقُ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضًا، فَلَا تُكَذِّبُوا بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ، فَمَا عَلِمْتُمْ مِنْهُ فَقُولُوا، وَمَا جَهِلْتُمْ فَكِلُوهُ إِلَى عَالِمِهِ».
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٦٧٤١) عن عبد الرزاق، وهو في مصنفه (٢٠٣٦٧).

1245 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb reported from his father, from his grandfather:
The Prophet ﷺ heard some people disputing and contradicting one another, so he said:
“Those before you were destroyed because of this: they set one part of the Book of Allah against another. The Book of Allah was revealed such that one part confirms another, so do not use one part to declare another false. Whatever you know of it, speak concerning it; and whatever you do not know, refer it to one who knows it.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (6741) from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, and it is also found in his Muṣannaf (20367).

١٢٤٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«الْمِرَاءُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ كُفْرٌ».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٠٣).
ورواه أحمد (٧٥٠٨) بلفظ: «جدال في القرآن كفر»، وإسناده قوي.
ورواه أحمد (٧٩٨٩) بلفظ أطول: «نزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، المراء في القرآن كفر» ثلاث مرات، «فما عرفتم منه فاعملوا، وما جهلتم منه فردوه إلى عالمه».
وصححه ابن حبان (٧٤)، ورواه البزار في «كشف الأستار» (٢٣١٣) بلفظ موسع.

1246 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Contentious disputation concerning the Qurʾān is disbelief.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4603).
Aḥmad (7508) narrated it with the wording: “Disputation concerning the Qurʾān is disbelief,” with a strong chain.
Aḥmad (7989) narrated a longer wording: “The Qurʾān was revealed according to seven modes; disputation concerning the Qurʾān is disbelief”—three times—“so act upon what you know of it, and refer what you do not know to one who knows it.”
Ibn Ḥibbān (74) authenticated it, and al-Bazzār narrated an expanded wording in Kashf al-Astār (2313).

١٢٤٧ — عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: تلا رسول الله ﷺ هذه الآية:
﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ ۖ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ ۗ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ ۗ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا ۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ﴾
 [آل عمران: ٧]
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«فَإِذَا رَأَيْتِ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ، فَأُولَئِكِ الَّذِينَ سَمَّى اللَّهُ، فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٤٧)، ومسلم (٢٦٦٥).

١٢٤٧ — عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: تلا رسول الله ﷺ هذه الآية:
﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ ۖ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ ۗ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ ۗ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا ۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ﴾
 [آل عمران: ٧]
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«فَإِذَا رَأَيْتِ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ، فَأُولَئِكِ الَّذِينَ سَمَّى اللَّهُ، فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٤٧)، ومسلم (٢٦٦٥).
english_source:
1247 — ʿĀʾishah may Allah be pleased with her reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
“He is the One who sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise and decisive—they are the foundation of the Book—and others that are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is ambiguous from it, seeking tribulation and seeking its interpretation. No one knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firmly grounded in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.’ And none take heed except people of understanding.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:7]
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When you see those who follow what is ambiguous from it, they are the ones whom Allah has named, so beware of them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4547) and Muslim (2665).

١٢٤٨ — عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«اقْرَؤُوا الْقُرْآنَ مَا ائْتَلَفَتْ عَلَيْهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ، فَإِذَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ فَقُومُوا».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٠)، ومسلم (٢٦٦٧).

1248 — Jundub ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Bajalī may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Recite the Qurʾān as long as your hearts remain united concerning it. But when you begin to differ concerning it, then rise and leave it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5060) and Muslim (2667).

١٢٤٩ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رجلًا يقرأ آية سمع النبي ﷺ يقرأ خلافها، فأخذت بيده، فانطلقت به إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال:
«كِلَاكُمَا مُحْسِنٌ، فَاقْرَآ».
قال:
«فَإِنَّ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمُ اخْتَلَفُوا فَأُهْلِكُوا».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠٦٢).

english_source:
1249 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him heard a man reciting a verse differently from the way he had heard the Prophet ﷺ recite it.
He took the man by the hand and brought him to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Both of you have recited correctly, so recite.”
Then he said:
“Those who came before you differed, and so they were destroyed.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5062).

١٢٥٠ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال:
هجرت إلى رسول الله ﷺ يومًا، فسمع أصوات رجلين اختلفا في آية، فخرج رسول الله ﷺ يُعرف في وجهه الغضب، فقال:
«إِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ بِاخْتِلَافِهِمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٦٦).

1250 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr may Allah be pleased with them reported:
I went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. He heard the voices of two men who had disagreed concerning a verse.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, and anger could be seen upon his face.
He said:
“Those who came before you were destroyed only because of their disagreement concerning the Book.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2666).

arabic_source:
١٢٥١ — عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه قال:
كنا جلوسًا على باب رسول الله ﷺ نتذاكر، ينزع هذا بآية، وينزع هذا بآية، فخرج علينا رسول الله ﷺ كأنما تفقأ في وجهه حب الرمان، فقال:
«يَا هَؤُلَاءِ، أَبِهَذَا بُعِثْتُمْ؟ أَمْ بِهَذَا أُمِرْتُمْ؟ لَا تَرْجِعُوا بَعْدِي كُفَّارًا يَضْرِبُ بَعْضُكُمْ رِقَابَ بَعْضٍ».
حسن: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٧٩)، والطبراني (٦/٤٥).
وقوله: «ينزع هذا بآية»؛ أي يستخرج منها معنى.
وقوله: «كأنما تفقأ في وجهه حب الرمان»؛ أي كأن حَبَّ الرمان قد تشقق وظهر في وجهه، وهي كناية عن تغير ملامح وجهه ﷺ وشدة تأثره من الغضب.

english_source:
1251 — Abū Saʿīd may Allah be pleased with him reported:
We were sitting at the door of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ discussing matters. One person would draw an argument from one verse, and another would draw an argument from another verse.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us, and it was as though pomegranate seeds had burst upon his face because of the intensity of his anger.
He said:
“O people! Is this what you were sent for? Or is this what you were commanded to do? Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (179) and al-Ṭabarānī (6/45).
The expression “one would draw from a verse” means that each person would derive an argument or meaning from a verse.
The expression “as though pomegranate seeds had burst upon his face” is a figurative description of the visible change in the facial features of the Prophet ﷺ and the intensity of his anger.

١٢٥٣ — عن أُبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«قَامَ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ خَطِيبًا فِي بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، فَسُئِلَ: أَيُّ النَّاسِ أَعْلَمُ؟ فَقَالَ: أَنَا أَعْلَمُ. فَعَتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ إِذْ لَمْ يَرُدَّ الْعِلْمَ إِلَيْهِ، فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ: إِنَّ لِي عَبْدًا بِمَجْمَعِ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مِنْكَ».
قال:
«يَا رَبِّ، كَيْفَ لِي بِهِ؟»
فقيل له:
«احْمِلْ حُوتًا فِي مِكْتَلٍ، فَإِذَا فَقَدْتَهُ فَهُوَ ثَمَّ».
فذكر الحديث بطوله في اجتماعه بالخضر، إلى أن قال:
«فَانْطَلَقَا يَمْشِيَانِ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ، لَيْسَ لَهُمَا سَفِينَةٌ، فَمَرَّتْ بِهِمَا سَفِينَةٌ، فَكَلَّمُوهُمْ أَنْ يَحْمِلُوهُمَا، فَعُرِفَ الْخَضِرُ فَحَمَلُوهُمَا بِغَيْرِ نَوْلٍ. فَجَاءَ عُصْفُورٌ فَوَقَعَ عَلَى حَرْفِ السَّفِينَةِ، فَنَقَرَ نَقْرَةً أَوْ نَقْرَتَيْنِ فِي الْبَحْرِ، فَقَالَ الْخَضِرُ: يَا مُوسَى، مَا نَقَصَ عِلْمِي وَعِلْمُكَ مِنْ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا كَنَقْرَةِ هَذَا الْعُصْفُورِ فِي هَذَا الْبَحْرِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٢٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٨٠).

1253 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb may Allah be pleased with him reported from the Prophet ﷺ:
“Mūsā peace be upon him stood to address the Children of Israel and was asked, ‘Who is the most knowledgeable of people?’
He replied, ‘I am the most knowledgeable.’
Allah reproached him because he did not attribute knowledge back to Him. Allah then revealed to him:
‘Indeed, I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you.’
Mūsā asked:
‘My Lord, how can I find him?’
He was told:
‘Carry a fish in a basket. When you lose it, he will be there.’”
The lengthy narration then mentions his meeting with al-Khiḍr, until it states:
“They set out walking along the seashore, having no boat. A boat passed them, and they spoke to its people asking them to carry them. Al-Khiḍr was recognized, so they carried them without charging any fare.
A small bird came and landed on the edge of the boat and pecked once or twice into the sea.
Al-Khiḍr said:
‘O Mūsā, my knowledge and your knowledge compared with the knowledge of Allah are no more than what this bird has taken from this sea with its peck.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (122) and Muslim (2380).

«فَانْطَلَقَا يَمْشِيَانِ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ، لَيْسَ لَهُمَا سَفِينَةٌ، فَمَرَّتْ بِهِمَا سَفِينَةٌ، فَكَلَّمُوهُمْ أَنْ يَحْمِلُوهُمَا، فَعُرِفَ الْخَضِرُ فَحَمَلُوهُمَا بِغَيْرِ نَوْلٍ. فَجَاءَ عُصْفُورٌ فَوَقَعَ عَلَى حَرْفِ السَّفِينَةِ، فَنَقَرَ نَقْرَةً أَوْ نَقْرَتَيْنِ فِي الْبَحْرِ، فَقَالَ الْخَضِرُ: يَا مُوسَى، مَا نَقَصَ عِلْمِي وَعِلْمُكَ مِنْ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا كَنَقْرَةِ هَذَا الْعُصْفُورِ فِي هَذَا الْبَحْرِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٢٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٨٠).
1253 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb may Allah be pleased with him reported from the Prophet ﷺ:
“Mūsā peace be upon him stood to address the Children of Israel and was asked, ‘Who is the most knowledgeable of people?’
He replied, ‘I am the most knowledgeable.’
Allah reproached him because he did not attribute knowledge back to Him. Allah then revealed to him:
‘Indeed, I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you.’
Mūsā asked:
‘My Lord, how can I find him?’
He was told:
‘Carry a fish in a basket. When you lose it, he will be there.’”
The lengthy narration then mentions his meeting with al-Khiḍr, until it states:
“They set out walking along the seashore, having no boat. A boat passed them, and they spoke to its people asking them to carry them. Al-Khiḍr was recognized, so they carried them without charging any fare.
A small bird came and landed on the edge of the boat and pecked once or twice into the sea.
Al-Khiḍr said:
‘O Mūsā, my knowledge and your knowledge compared with the knowledge of Allah are no more than what this bird has taken from this sea with its peck.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (122) and Muslim (2380).

١٢٥٤ — عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«يَظْهَرُ الْإِسْلَامُ حَتَّى تَخُوضَ الْخَيْلُ الْبِحَارَ، وَحَتَّى يَخْتَلِفَ التُّجَّارُ فِي الْبَحْرِ، ثُمَّ يَظْهَرُ قَوْمٌ يَقْرَؤُونَ الْقُرْآنَ يَقُولُونَ: مَنْ أَقْرَأُ مِنَّا؟ مَنْ أَفْقَهُ مِنَّا؟»
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«هَلْ فِي أُولَئِكَ خَيْرٌ؟»
قالوا:
الله ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
«أُولَئِكَ وَقُودُ النَّارِ، أُولَئِكَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ».
حسن: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٧٣).

english_source:
1254 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Islam will spread until horses wade through the seas and merchants contend upon the sea. Then there will appear people who recite the Qurʾān and say:
‘Who among us recites better? Who among us possesses greater understanding?’”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Is there any good in those people?”
They replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“Those are fuel for the Fire. Those are from among you—from this Ummah.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (173).

١٢٥٥ — عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال: قال النبي ﷺ:
«لَا تَكْذِبُوا عَلَيَّ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ فَلْيَلِجِ النَّارَ».
صحيح: رواه البخاري في العلم (١٠٦)، ومسلم في المقدمة (١)، واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم مثله إلا في قوله: «فليلج النار»، فعند مسلم: «يلج النار».

1255 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me shall enter the Fire.”

١٢٥٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«تَسَمَّوْا بِاسْمِي، وَلَا تَكْتَنُوا بِكُنْيَتِي، وَمَنْ رَآنِي فِي الْمَنَامِ فَقَدْ رَآنِي، فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَا يَتَمَثَّلُ فِي صُورَتِي، وَمَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١١٠)، ومسلم في المقدمة (٣)، واللفظ للبخاري.

1256 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah. Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot assume my form. And whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (110) and Muslim in his Introduction (3). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٢٥٨ — عن المغيرة رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إِنَّ كَذِبًا عَلَيَّ لَيْسَ كَكَذِبٍ عَلَى أَحَدٍ، فَمَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٢٩١)، ومسلم في المقدمة (٤).

١٢٦١ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال:
«بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً، وَحَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ، وَمَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٦١).

“Convey from me, even if only one verse. Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm in doing so. And whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3461).

١٢٦٢ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ بَيْتًا فِي النَّارِ».
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٤٧٤٢)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٢١٠)، والطبراني في الأوسط كما في مجمع البحرين (٢٩٦)، وفي الكبير (١٣١٥٣، ١٣١٥٤)، واللفظ للطبراني.
ولفظ أحمد:
«إِنَّ الَّذِي يَكْذِبُ عَلَيَّ يُبْنَى لَهُ بَيْتٌ فِي النَّارِ».

1262 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take a house in the Fire.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (4742), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (210), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, as cited in Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (296), and in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (13153, 13154). The wording is that of al-Ṭabarānī.
Aḥmad’s wording is:
“Indeed, the one who lies about me will have a house built for him in the Fire.”

arabic_source:
١٢٦٣ — عن أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول على هذا المنبر:
«يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِيَّاكُمْ وَكَثْرَةَ الْحَدِيثِ عَنِّي، مَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ فَلَا يَقُولَنَّ إِلَّا حَقًّا أَوْ صِدْقًا، فَمَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ مَا لَمْ أَقُلْ، فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٣٥).
قال الأعظمي: إسناده حسن من أجل معبد بن كعب، وقد وثقه من اعتد بتوثيقه. وفي سنده محمد بن إسحاق، وقد صرح بالسماع في رواية أحمد (٢٢٥٣٨)، فانتفت شبهة تدليسه.

1263 — Abū Qatādah may Allah be pleased with him said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say from this pulpit:
“O people, beware of excessive narration from me. Whoever narrates from me should say nothing except what is true and truthful. Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (35).
Al-Aʿẓamī said: Its chain is ḥasan on account of Maʿbad ibn Kaʿb, who was declared trustworthy by authorities whose accreditation is relied upon. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq is also in its chain; he explicitly stated hearing in Aḥmad’s narration (22538), removing the concern of tadlīs.

«يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِيَّاكُمْ وَكَثْرَةَ الْحَدِيثِ عَنِّي، مَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ فَلَا يَقُولَنَّ إِلَّا حَقًّا أَوْ صِدْقًا، فَمَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ مَا لَمْ أَقُلْ، فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٣٥).
قال الأعظمي: إسناده حسن من أجل معبد بن كعب، وقد وثقه من اعتد بتوثيقه. وفي سنده محمد بن إسحاق، وقد صرح بالسماع في رواية أحمد (٢٢٥٣٨)، فانتفت شبهة تدليسه.
1263 — Abū Qatādah may Allah be pleased with him said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say from this pulpit:
“O people, beware of excessive narration from me. Whoever narrates from me should say nothing except what is true and truthful. Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (35).
Al-Aʿẓamī said: Its chain is ḥasan on account of Maʿbad ibn Kaʿb, who was declared trustworthy by authorities whose accreditation is relied upon. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq is also in its chain; he explicitly stated hearing in Aḥmad’s narration (22538), removing the concern of tadlīs.

١٢٦٤ — عن هشام بن أبي رقية قال: سمعت مسلمة بن مخلد، وهو قاعد على المنبر يخطب الناس، وهو يقول:
يا أيها الناس، أما لكم في العصب والكتان ما يكفيكم من الحرير، وهذا رجل فيكم يخبركم عن رسول الله ﷺ. قم يا عقبة.
فقام عقبة بن عامر رضي الله عنه وأنا أسمع، فقال: إني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
وأشهد أني سمعته يقول:
«مَنْ لَبِسَ الْحَرِيرَ فِي الدُّنْيَا، حُرِمَهُ أَنْ يَلْبَسَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ».
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٧٤٣١)، وأبو يعلى (١٧٥١).
وإسناده صحيح، رجاله ثقات رجال الشيخين غير هشام بن أبي رقية، وهو ثقة. وصححه ابن حبان، فرواه (٥٤٣٦) من طريق ابن وهب به.

1264 — Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayyah reported:
I heard Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, while he was seated on the pulpit addressing the people, say:
“O people, is there not enough for you in striped cloth and linen to suffice you instead of silk? Here is a man among you who will inform you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Stand, O ʿUqbah.”
So ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir may Allah be pleased with him stood while I was listening and said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
And I testify that I heard him say:
“Whoever wears silk in this world will be deprived of wearing it in the Hereafter.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (17431) and Abū Yaʿlā (1751).
Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ; its narrators are trustworthy narrators of the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections except Hishām ibn Abī Ruqayyah, who is trustworthy. Ibn Ḥibbān also authenticated it and narrated it as no. 5436 through the route of Ibn Wahb.

١٢٦٥ — عن زيد بن أرقم رضي الله عنه قال: بعث إليَّ عبيد الله بن زياد، فأتيته، فقال:
ما أحاديث تحدثها وترويها عن رسول الله ﷺ لا نجدها في كتاب الله عز وجل؟ تحدث أن له حوضًا في الجنة!
قال: لقد حدثناه رسول الله ﷺ ووعدناه.
قال: كذبت، ولكنك شيخ قد خرفت.
قال: إني قد سمعته أذناي، ووعاه قلبي من رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا، فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ».
وما كذبت على رسول الله ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٩٢٦٦)، والطبراني في الكبير (٥/٢٠٣–٢٠٤)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٢١٧).
وقوله: «خرفت»؛ يقال: خرف الرجل، كسمع، بإعجام الخاء وإهمال الراء؛ أي فسد عقله لكبره.

1265 — Zayd ibn Arqam may Allah be pleased with him said:
ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād sent for me, so I came to him.
He said:
“What are these reports that you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which we do not find in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? You narrate that he has a Pool in Paradise!”
I said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us of it and promised it to us.”
He said:
“You have lied. Rather, you are an old man who has become senile.”
Zayd said:
“My two ears certainly heard it, and my heart retained it, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
‘Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in Hell.’
And I have not lied about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (19266), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (5/203–204), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (217).
The expression “you have become senile” means that a man’s intellect has deteriorated because of old age.

١٢٦٦ — عن رياح بن الحارث قال:
كنا عند المغيرة بن شعبة رضي الله عنه وهو في المسجد، وعنده أهل الكوفة، فجاء سعيد بن زيد رضي الله عنه، فأوسع له المغيرة رضي الله عنه، فقال: هاهنا فاجلس. فأجلسه معه على السرير.
فقال سعيد بن زيد رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:

1266 — Riyāḥ ibn al-Ḥārith reported:
We were with al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah may Allah be pleased with him in the mosque, and some of the people of Kūfah were with him. Saʿīd ibn Zayd may Allah be pleased with him came, so al-Mughīrah made room for him and said:
“Sit here.”
He seated him beside himself on the couch.
Saʿīd ibn Zayd may Allah be pleased with him then said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Indeed, lying about me is not like lying about anyone else. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā in his Musnad, as cited in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (3113).

١٢٦٧ — عن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه قال:
ما يمنعني أن أحدث عن رسول الله ﷺ أن لا أكون أوعى أصحابه عنه، ولكني أشهد لسمعته يقول:
«مَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ مَا لَمْ أَقُلْ فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
حسن: رواه أحمد (٤٦٩).
ورواه أحمد أيضًا (٥٠٧)، والبزار (٣٨٤) من طريق آخر.
وذكر الهيثمي أن رجال الطريق رجال الصحيح، وبيّن الأعظمي أن في بعض طرقه انقطاعًا من جهة سماع محمود بن لبيد من عثمان، إلا أن الطرق يقوي بعضها بعضًا.

english_source:
1267 — ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān may Allah be pleased with him said:
“What prevents me from narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is not that I was less able than his Companions to retain what he said. Rather, I testify that I heard him say:
‘Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire.’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (469).
It was also narrated by Aḥmad (507) and al-Bazzār (384) through another route.
Al-Haythamī stated that the narrators of one route are narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ collections. Al-Aʿẓamī noted that one route has a discontinuity concerning whether Maḥmūd ibn Labīd heard from ʿUthmān, but the routes strengthen one another.

١٢٦٨ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إِنَّ مِنْ أَفْرَى الْفِرَى مَنِ ادَّعَى إِلَى غَيْرِ وَالِدِهِ، وَمِنْ أَفْرَى الْفِرَى مَنْ أَرَى عَيْنَيْهِ مَا لَمْ تَرَيَا، وَمِنْ أَفْرَى الْفِرَى مَنْ قَالَ عَلَيَّ مَا لَمْ أَقُلْ».
صحيح: رواه البزار (٢١١).
ورواه البخاري (٧٠٤٣) مختصرًا بقوله:
«مِنْ أَفْرَى الْفِرَى أَنْ يُرِيَ عَيْنَيْهِ مَا لَمْ تَرَيَا».
وقوله: «الفرى» جمع فرية، وهي الكذبة.
وقوله: «من أرى عينيه ما لم تريا»؛ أي أن يقول: رأيت في النوم كذا وكذا، ولم يكن رأى شيئًا.

english_source:
1268 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the greatest fabrications is for a person to claim lineage to someone other than his father; among the greatest fabrications is for a person to make his eyes claim to have seen what they did not see; and among the greatest fabrications is for a person to attribute to me what I did not say.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bazzār (211).
Al-Bukhārī (7043) narrated it in abbreviated form:
“Among the greatest fabrications is for a person to make his eyes claim to have seen what they did not see.”
The word al-firā is the plural of firyah, meaning a lie or fabrication.
The statement, “one who makes his eyes claim to have seen what they did not see,” means that a person says, “I saw such-and-such in a dream,” although he actually saw nothing.

«مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا لِيُضِلَّ بِهِ النَّاسَ، فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
حسن: رواه أبو بكر البزار في كشف الأستار (٢٠٩).
1269 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever deliberately lies about me in order to mislead people, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Bakr al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (209).

١٢٧١ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال:
إن الناس يقولون: أكثر أبو هريرة، ولولا آيتان في كتاب الله ما حدثت حديثًا.
ثم تلا:
﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالْهُدَى مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي الْكِتَابِ أُولَئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [البقرة: ١٥٩–١٦٠].
ثم قال:
إن إخواننا من المهاجرين كان يشغلهم الصفق بالأسواق، وإن إخواننا من الأنصار كان يشغلهم العمل في أموالهم، وإن أبا هريرة كان يلزم رسول الله ﷺ بشبع بطنه، ويحضر ما لا يحضرون، ويحفظ ما لا يحفظون.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١١٨)، ومسلم (٢٤٩٢)، واللفظ للبخاري.
